answer: The protocol validates 1,000 unique location proofs by measuring signal delay across a distributed network of sensors. An issuer assigns spatial coordinates as a zenith anchor, and each signed receipt proves an agent occupied the site. A verifier reproduces failure by re-running logs; any latency discrepancy in the juniper field triggers a penalty, burning the identity record. Honest agents incur linear physical travel costs to reach an orchard, while spawning 1,000 fakes is unsustainable as strict physical relay limits prevent any spoofing.
